name: ShadePass (merged: Blind Gift + ShadePass): gift a shade without seeing their face
one_liner: Gifting with privacy built in. The giver shortlists 2-4 lip or foundation shades and sends a deep link over iMessage or WhatsApp. The recipient tries them privately on their own phone with YouCam and picks one. The giver gets back only the chosen SKU: no photo, skin hex or scores.
target_user: People buying lip or complexion products for someone else (partners, friends, family), and recipients who want a shade that fits without sharing a selfie.
buyer: Shopper (giver and recipient). Retailer angle: a 'gift with shade-check' button for a brand or e-tailer gift flow. Any reduction in wrong-shade gift returns is a hypothesis, not a measured result.
core_flow: 1) The giver picks a product type and shortlists 2-4 shades (or a whole range) from a seeded catalog, then sends a deep link through the native share sheet. 2) The recipient opens it and sees a plain-language consent screen listing exactly what the giver will and won't receive, with deletion after 24h and a 'decline' option that tells the giver nothing about the reason. 3) Guided selfie with on-device face gating (face >60% width, frontal, even light) and haptic or voice cues, then a presigned PUT straight to YouCam. 4) Facial Color Tones (skin and lip hex), plus optional Fitzpatrick used only for a limits note, and Makeup VTO tasks in parallel for each shade, side by side with a deterministic CIEDE2000 closeness bar labelled 'cosmetic preview'. 5) The recipient picks one, or chooses 'none fit, send the full range or a gift card'; if no shade is under the closeness threshold, the app says so. 6) The giver gets a push: 'Shade 2 chosen: <SKU>' plus a privacy receipt of what was not shared. The recipient's local images are purged and both sides get a deletion confirmation.
youcam_apis: File upload (POST /s2s/v2.0/file, presigned PUT)
Facial Color Tones / Skin Tone Analysis (skin_color, lip color hex)
Makeup VTO (lip_color, foundation, blush with hex/texture/intensity), one task per shade in parallel
Fitzpatrick skin type (optional, only for a confidence/limits note)
Async task polling or webhook to a small relay that triggers the push
novelty_vs_competitors: Closest repos are single-user shade tools: guptachetan1995/shade-guard (checks cart foundation against the shopper's own face), noirithm/shadewise (shade-suit widget), Veerpratapgupta/GlowKart (lipstick match plus VTO), rishabhcli/tryproof, akhilsai132007/ShadeProof, raj921/ToneMatchApp (Expo shade matching), and consent-focused aryarahimi1/mirrorkey and hgyu-mech/tryon-compare. edycutjong/onedress is multi-person but pools data. Every existing tool assumes buyer and wearer are the same person. ShadePass splits them across two devices and withholds the face data from the payer. Grep: 0 gift repos.

name: GiftPass: try a gift on someone else, with their revocable consent
one_liner: The gift recipient sends the giver a private, time-limited try-on pass from their own phone. The giver can then try earrings, scarves, hats, lip shades and nails on the recipient's real photo without spoiling the surprise. The recipient can revoke the pass at any time, which deletes the tasks at YouCam.
target_user: Shoppers buying beauty or accessory gifts (lipstick, nail set, scarf, earrings, hat) for a partner, parent or friend, where color and face shape decide whether the gift works.
buyer: The gift-buying shopper uses it free. Accessory and beauty retailers would pay to embed a 'Try it on them' button on gift pages, aiming to raise confidence on pricier gifts and cut color-mismatch gift returns (a hypothesis).
core_flow: 1) The giver taps 'Ask for a GiftPass' and sends a deep link through the share sheet; the link does not reveal which item. 2) The recipient opens it, reads a one-screen e-consent (who is asking, which categories, 72h expiry, cap of 8 try-ons, no downloads), then takes a guided selfie and optionally a hand photo for nails. Only the recipient's live camera can capture, so there are no gallery uploads. 3) The backend uploads once (POST /file) and runs Facial Color Tones (skin, eye, lip and hair hex) and Face Attributes (face shape). Only the derived palette and face shape reach the giver. 4) The giver sees a small catalog ranked by that palette and face shape with a 'why' chip (e.g. 'warm lip hex, so coral over blue-red'). Each tap runs a real task on the recipient's photo: Makeup VTO lip_color, Earring VTO, Scarf VTO, Hat VTO or Nail VTO. Results are watermarked and screenshots are deterred. 5) The recipient's app shows only '3 of 8 try-ons used', never what was tried. 6) Revoke or expiry deletes every task and uploaded file and clears the giver's gallery. The gift ships with a 'picked for your coloring' card and nearby-shade exchange options.
youcam_apis: File upload (POST /s2s/v2.0/file, presigned PUT)
Facial Color Tones / Skin Tone Analysis
Face Attributes & Ratio (face shape)
Makeup VTO (lip_color, blush)
Earring VTO
Scarf VTO
Hat VTO
Nail VTO
Task deletion endpoint for revocation (ideator-reported as /s2s/v2.0/task/delete; not in evidence.md, so verify in docs in hour 1)
novelty_vs_competitors: Closest: Moyo-Made/asolink (guests see aso ebi fabric on themselves, a group self try-on), edycutjong/onedress (bridesmaids each try on themselves), RohanGlitched/hairloom ('sealed fitter links' for wig fitters), aryarahimi1/mirrorkey (consent-native appearance compute), FitReceipt and KeepMe (consent for self try-on), ctmakc/babakokum-tryon (Scarf VTO + Color Tones, self). No repo lets one person try products on another consenting person. The new parts are a two-party consent model with a blind surprise (the recipient sees the count, not the items) and revocation wired to real API task deletion. Distinct from C1 ShadePass, where the giver never sees renders; here the giver browses and the recipient keeps control.

name: Counter (merged: Counter + CounterClean): beauty-advisor phone that hands off results and wipes itself
one_liner: An in-store clienteling app for beauty advisors. The customer gives e-consent and the phone gates capture on-device. The advisor scans shelf SKUs to try them on the customer's face, hands results to the customer's own phone by QR, then purges the device and shows a timestamped wipe receipt. The retailer keeps a consent audit log with no face data.
target_user: Beauty advisors and associates at specialty, department-store and drugstore counters doing consults on a shared store phone or tablet, and the walk-in customers they serve, who need no app or account.
buyer: Retailer. It buys the tool for associates to run consults designed around BIPA guidance that lead to a sale. The shopper keeps their own results without an account.
core_flow: 1) The advisor taps New Consult. The customer reads and ticks a plain-language e-consent on the counter phone: what is captured, that YouCam processes it, that results expire on YouCam within 24h, nothing linked to a name. 2) Live camera with on-device face detection enables the shutter only when face >60% width, frontal and evenly lit. A haptic tick fires per condition met and a double pulse on auto-capture, so no units are wasted. 3) A presigned PUT, then parallel async tasks: Facial Color Tones (skin hex), SD Skin Analysis on a 4-concern subset with mask overlay, and optional Fitzpatrick for a limits note. Results show as cosmetic-appearance bands, not verdict scores. 4) The advisor scans 3-5 shelf barcodes (seeded catalog SKU to hex/texture). Each scan fires a Makeup VTO task (foundation or lip_color) and a side-by-side grid fills as tasks land. 5) Hand-off QR (or AirDrop): the customer opens a tokenized, cookie-free page with their looks and SKU list that expires in 24h. 6) End Consult purges the photo, cache and task IDs and shows a wipe receipt. The retailer log records only the consent version hash, timestamp, SKUs previewed and purchase yes/no.
youcam_apis: File upload (POST /s2s/v2.0/file, presigned PUT)
Facial Color Tones / Skin Tone Analysis
Skin Analysis v2.1 SD (subset, e.g. oiliness, moisture, redness, texture; mask PNG overlays; 9+ units)
Makeup VTO (foundation, concealer, lip_color with hex/texture/intensity)
Fitzpatrick skin type (optional, confidence/limits note only)
Async task polling or webhook to the proxy
novelty_vs_competitors: Closest: Balu-SG/shelfmatch and DesignMaster-Solutions/shelf-check (store-catalog selfie match, web, shopper-driven), Noufalthecoder/ShelfSense (shopper-side AR barcode lens with ingredient verdicts), JonathanSolvesProblems/swatchless (hair-color retail desk, web), AsafMeizner/skintrace and bisale24-ops/same-light (capture-condition checks), aryarahimi1/mirrorkey, praveenkumar5151/goodskin-youcam-hackathon and code-up-matrix/fitreceipt-devpost-2026 (consent-first, single user). None puts an associate-operated native app on the sales floor with a consent, handoff and wipe lifecycle on a shared device, plus a retailer audit log with no face data. Barcode scanning overlaps ShelfSense mechanically but runs retailer-side and drives VTO.

name: LiveSwatch (merged: LiveSwatch + Said & Shown): shade-range cards and claim linting for phone live sellers
one_liner: A host co-pilot for beauty and fashion sellers who stream from a phone. Before the show it pre-renders each SKU on a consented, measured skin-tone panel with YouCam. During the show it pops the matching render card when a viewer asks 'how does Berry look on deep skin?', and lints the host's pitch for drug-like or 'works on everyone' claims.
target_user: Small live-commerce sellers, boutique hosts and creators selling lipstick, foundation, blush or tops via phone livestreams (TikTok Shop / Whatnot / Instagram Live style), plus brand teams who brief affiliates.
buyer: Retailer/seller, per show or per month. Value: faster answers to tone questions, fairer shade representation, fewer misleading-claim problems, and a post-show report of which tone bands viewers asked about that the seller's imagery doesn't cover.
core_flow: 1) Run-of-show setup: the seller adds tonight's 5-8 SKUs by photo, CSV or catalog with hex, texture and category. 2) Tone panel: enrol 4-6 consenting team members or creators once. Facial Color Tones and Fitzpatrick measure each person, and the panel is labelled by measured tone band, not a guess. 3) Pre-render every SKU x panel pair via Makeup VTO (lip_color, blush, foundation) or cloth-v4 through the async File/task flow, with a progress grid. Each SKU gets a Shade Range Card: renders plus a deterministic CIEDE2000 contrast metric (shade vs measured skin) and plain labels like 'reads sheer on deeper skin'. 4) Live mode: a pasted or simulated comment feed is parsed into SKU + tone band, and the matching card jumps to the top of a one-thumb queue (haptic, tap to show full screen or push as an overlay). Fit or size questions get an honest canned reply. 5) Claim linter: the host's typed or on-device-dictated pitch is checked by rules. Drug claims ('clears breakouts') get cosmetic rewrites ('helps the look of'), and universality claims ('works on everyone') are cross-checked against the card. 6) Post-show report: tone-band demand vs panel coverage, cards shown, short-link clicks, plus a hash/input record per card and lint decision for brand audit.
youcam_apis: File API (presigned upload) + async task polling/webhooks
Makeup VTO (lip_color, blush, foundation, eye_shadow with hex/texture/intensity)
Clothes VTO cloth-v4 (upper/full) for apparel SKUs
Facial Color Tones analyzer (panel measurement, contrast metric)
Fitzpatrick skin type (panel labelling)
novelty_vs_competitors: The multi-tone panel mechanic is not new: fiya-chris-and-AI/casting (garment on 8 measured skin types) and round-1 winner ShadeSpan (catalog on 6 Fitzpatrick tones). Say so. StephenSook/aloud used a CI claim linter internally; StuartYo/youcam-claim-guard and amydojo/face-value check skin-improvement claims against measurement noise. Grep for live/stream/seller finds no live-commerce tool (live-beauty-score is a single-user AR scoring toy; ShermaineYap/sopan is an async seller agent). LiveSwatch differs because it targets the real-time live moment rather than catalog QA, answers specific viewer questions, covers makeup as well as apparel, adds a user-facing cosmetic-vs-drug linter cross-checked against the renders, and runs as a native phone host console.

name: DropLive: an 'on me' second screen for live shopping viewers
one_liner: When a live seller drops a lip shade, earrings or a top on stream, every consenting viewer's phone instantly reveals that product on their own face or body, ranked against their measured coloring. The seller gets an aggregate try-to-cart panel with no faces in it.
target_user: Viewers of beauty and fashion live-shopping streams run by small sellers, indie brands and boutique owners who sell live from a phone.
buyer: Retailers and live sellers pay per session or per seat for the aggregate analytics. Viewers use it free.
core_flow: 1) The viewer joins a stream room by code or QR, reads a one-screen e-consent, and takes one guided selfie (plus a full-body photo if apparel is in the drop). Each image is uploaded once and its file id is reused for every drop. 2) At join, Facial Color Tones runs once to get skin, lip and hair hex. 3) Just after join, the viewer's phone pre-renders the whole drop queue in the background (Makeup VTO lip_color, Earring VTO, cloth-v4). 4) The host's phone shows the drop queue (e.g. four lip shades, two earrings, one top), and tapping Drop pushes the SKU to all viewers over a realtime channel (Supabase or Firebase). The drop reveals an existing render, so there is no wait. 5) The viewer gets a haptic tap and an 'On you' card beside the stream with a deterministic CIEDE2000 'contrast with your lips/skin' chip, labelled a preview, and a one-tap cart. 6) The host sees live aggregate tries and try-to-cart per SKU and skipped shades, with a minimum group size and no images.
youcam_apis: File upload (POST /s2s/v2.0/file), file id reused across drops
Facial Color Tones / Skin Tone Analysis
Makeup VTO (lip_color, eye_shadow, blush)
Earring VTO (optionally Necklace VTO)
Clothes VTO cloth-v4 (upper, auto)
Async task polling or webhooks for background pre-render
novelty_vs_competitors: Grep for live, stream, seller, tiktok, creator and influencer finds no live-commerce try-on. Hits are unrelated: fokrulanthro16-eng/retailmind-ai (single-user 'live' skin telemetry), swathigampa354-ship-it/live-beauty-score (single-user AR scoring), Balu-SG/shelfmatch (seller gap insights, no live event), ShermaineYap/sopan (async seller agent). Closest in spirit is Moyo-Made/asolink (one link, many guests self try-on). DropLive is new in three ways: one host event triggers many personal renders at once, pre-rendering makes the drop instant, and host analytics are aggregate-only. It is viewer-side, the complement of C4 (host-side).

name: Silver Mirror: a large-type beauty fitting room for shoppers 55+
one_liner: A large-type, one-thumb beauty fitting room for shoppers 55+. It reads mature-skin concerns with HD Skin Analysis and shows the same shade twice: once applied as in the ad, once adjusted for this face, with a reason for every change and no age verdict.
target_user: Women 55+ who buy foundation, concealer, lip and eye products online and feel products aren't made for them, many of them new to buying beauty online.
buyer: Mainly the shopper (free app with affiliate or retailer cart). Secondary: beauty retailers or brands licensing a 'mature-skin try-on' module for a demographic they underserve.
core_flow: 1) Consent screen in 20pt+ type with optional read-aloud. Capture uses a large face-width and light guide and a voice or tap shutter. 2) HD Skin Analysis returns hd_wrinkle, hd_firmness, droopy eyelid, tear_trough, age_spot and moisture with mask overlays. skin_age and the overall score are hidden by design. Facial Color Tones returns skin and lip colour. 3) A transparent rules table maps concerns to technique: low moisture -> satin, lower-intensity foundation; age_spot regions -> spot concealer; droopy eyelid -> thinner liner and softer shadow. 4) Makeup VTO renders two looks side by side in the same shade, 'as in the ad' (full intensity, matte) and 'tuned for you', each change with a one-line reason tied to a ui_score. 5) Big-button cart of 2-3 items and 'Send to my daughter/friend' via the share sheet. Photos are deleted after the 24h result window.
youcam_apis: File upload + async task/poll flow (/s2s/v2.0/file, /task/<feature>)
Skin Analysis v2.1 HD (hd_wrinkle, hd_firmness, droopy eyelid, tear_trough, age_spot, moisture, mask PNGs)
Facial Color Tones
Makeup VTO (foundation, concealer, eyeliner, eye_shadow, lip_color with texture + intensity)
Hair color VTO (optional grey-blending stretch goal)
novelty_vs_competitors: Grep for senior, mature, older, elder and menopause: 0 hits. Closest: swathigampa354-ship-it/face-ahead and yashwanth07-debug/skinforge (Aging Simulation showing younger users a future face, the opposite direction), adrian539859/coverkind-proof ('lightest sufficient coverage', no age focus or technique adaptation), yadneshSalvi/steady (motor-adaptive makeup guidance), sh0sub/mirror-tutor (K-beauty technique). Silver Mirror is new in three ways: it is designed for an ignored demographic, it compares the ad look with the adjusted look in the same shade, and it hides skin_age on purpose.

name: SeatedFit: try-on for wheelchair users, with an honest seated-reliability label
one_liner: Virtual try-on for wheelchair users and others who can't use a fitting room. A seated photo goes through Clothes VTO and accessory VTO, and each result is labelled 'previews well seated' or 'unreliable seated'. Retailers get a per-SKU seated-preview report.
target_user: Wheelchair users and people with limited mobility who buy clothes online because fitting rooms are too small or inaccessible, and the carers who often take the photo.
buyer: Shopper-facing app. Retailers pay for a 'Seated preview' badge and filter plus a per-SKU seated-render reliability report (similar in spirit to ShadeSpan's B2B audit, for body position instead of skin tone).
core_flow: 1) Accessible capture: the shopper or a carer takes a front-facing seated photo with a voice or timer shutter, with torso-in-frame guidance, after explicit e-consent; the photo is deleted after 24h. 2) Pick a garment from a seeded shop. Routing by category: upper and outerwear go to cloth-v4; scarf, hat, bag, watch and earrings go to their own endpoints, which render independently of posture. 3) Parallel async tasks with a progress UI. 4) A reliability check per result (category vs seated pose, task success, the user's thumbs up or down). Lower-body and full-length items are labelled 'unreliable seated: preview not shown' instead of showing a broken render. 5) An outfit board (top + scarf + bag) with 'preview, not a fit guarantee' copy. 6) A retailer view of which SKUs rendered acceptably on the team's seated test photos.
youcam_apis: File upload + async task/poll flow (parallel tasks)
AI Clothes VTO cloth-v4 (upper_body, outerwear; lower/full flagged)
Scarf VTO
Hat VTO
Bag VTO
Watch VTO
Earring/Necklace VTO
Generative background removal/change (optional, to clean cluttered home backgrounds)
novelty_vs_competitors: Grep for wheelchair, mobility and tremor: 0 hits. Closest: yadneshSalvi/steady (motor-adaptive makeup, not apparel), Perl58/ouchi-stylist (styling for people who find it hard to go out, no seated-pose handling), StephenSook/aloud and Abhinav0905/before-the-cut (blind/low-vision), chainwright/said-in-colour (colour-blind apparel), fiya-chris-and-AI/casting and ShadeSpan (multi-tone B2B). SeatedFit is the only one that treats a seated body as a first-class VTO input, measures where the API fails, and turns that into a retailer audit.

name: FirstShelf: teen skincare co-sign with parent consent and approval
one_liner: A teen-and-parent skincare checker. Before a teen's social-media 'haul' reaches checkout, a parent-consented skin scan checks each product against what the teen's skin actually shows and flags adult anti-aging actives. Makeup and nail try-ons give the teen something fun to buy instead.
target_user: Teens 13-17 (no under-13s, to stay out of COPPA) building skincare wishlists from social media, plus the parent who pays.
buyer: Parents get control, but the stronger buyer is the retailer: a brand-safe 'parent-approved cart' for teen shoppers.
core_flow: 1) The teen builds a wishlist by barcode or from a seeded catalog of about 30 products with ingredient lists. 2) A consent request goes to the parent's phone by deep link or QR. The parent gives explicit e-consent and sets a spending cap. No face is captured before this. 3) SD Skin Analysis on the teen (oiliness, moisture, redness, acne, pore, skin_type) returns masks and ui_scores. The selfie is deleted on return and nothing is tied to identity. 4) A deterministic check sorts each item into 'matches what your skin shows', 'not for your goal' (anti-aging retinol or AHA with no matching concern) or 'ask a dermatologist', citing the ui_score and the ingredient. 5) The teen swaps flagged spend for fun try-ons: low-intensity lip tint or blush (Makeup VTO) and nail colours (Nail VTO). 6) The parent gets an approval card with reasons, swaps and total vs cap, and approves or edits.
youcam_apis: File upload + async task/poll flow
Skin Analysis v2.1 SD (oiliness, moisture, redness, acne, pore, skin_type, masks)
Makeup VTO (lip_color, blush at low intensity)
Nail VTO
Facial Color Tones (lip/skin tone for tint shade)
novelty_vs_competitors: Grep for teen, adolescent and minor: 0 hits (the single 'parent' hit is unrelated). Closest: AnandUgale/skinshelf (scan literacy, before-you-buy receipts), Bowen1314/unstack (layering check), G-ojies/trueglow (flags mercury/hydroquinone), leesin1716-byte/shelf-check and tanishmisra9/receipts-skin ('buy less'), bodycount82/fit-check (budget refusal). None has a two-party consent model, age-appropriateness logic or a parent approval cart. The skin-scan-to-shop core is saturated (~35 repos), so pitch the consent and approval architecture and the swap-for-try-on, not the scan.

name: Polish Pocket: try the bottle on your nails, right in the aisle
one_liner: Scan a nail-polish bottle's barcode in a drugstore aisle, and YouCam Nail VTO paints that shade on a stored photo of your own hand in seconds. Swipe-compare up to 4 bottles, send a 'which one?' poll to a friend, and walk out with the right shade.
target_user: In-store shoppers choosing nail polish, where a sealed bottle can't be swatched before buying. Secondary: drugstore or beauty-retailer category managers.
buyer: Shopper first. Retailer angle: a white-label 'aisle try-on' with per-SKU scan-to-try analytics, pitched as a capability, not a measured lift.
core_flow: 1) In the aisle, the app opens to the scanner: the expo-camera barcode reader matches the UPC to a seeded catalog of about 20 polishes (hex + finish). A fallback eyedropper samples bottle color from the frame with a white-balance warning. 2) First time only: a guided hand photo with an on-screen hand outline and haptic confirmation, stored on-device for reuse. 3) Each scan triggers a Nail VTO task, with a progress ring and a haptic on completion. 4) Scan up to 4 bottles and swipe a carousel to compare on the same hand, with finish labels. 5) 'Ask a friend' sends a 4-up collage via the share sheet with a deep-link poll, and the vote comes back as a push. 6) A saved aisle list with SKU and shelf location, plus a buy-online fallback.
youcam_apis: File upload (presigned PUT)
Nail VTO (listed in evidence.md docs v1.17; input format, hex vs design template, still to be verified)
Optional: Skin Tone Analysis from a one-time selfie for color-harmony suggestions (labelled as such)
Optional: Makeup VTO lip_color for a 'match lips to nails' bonus
Async task polling
novelty_vs_competitors: Closest: TurnerCrypt/swatchroom (nail design fitting room with YouCam Nail VTO, web), Driedsandwich/colorway (one color across nails, lips, hair and outfit), Noufalthecoder/ShelfSense (live AR barcode lens in the aisle, but skincare ingredients and lipstick VTO, web). The aisle barcode mechanic isn't new (ShelfSense), so novelty rests on the category plus native execution: a native in-aisle trigger from a physical polish bottle, a reusable stored hand photo, and a friend-vote loop. Say this honestly.

name: Lineup: a first grooming kit for men from measured hair density, frizz and face shape
one_liner: For men new to grooming: one selfie measures hair density, frizz, face shape and skin oiliness. The app renders a 3x3 grid of hairstyle-plus-beard looks on the user's face by chaining YouCam outputs, then turns the chosen look into a kit of at most 3 products and a card to show the barber.
target_user: Men new to grooming and skincare, often first-time buyers, who don't know what suits them or what to buy.
buyer: Shopper free. Men's grooming retailers and DTC brands pay to convert new-to-category customers; barbershops could resell it white-label as a consultation app.
core_flow: 1) Guided front selfie (face >60% width, even light) with e-consent. 2) Parallel measurement: Face Attributes & Ratio (face shape and ratios), Hair Density Detection, Hair Frizziness Detection, and SD Skin Analysis limited to oiliness, pore, skin_type and redness. 3) A transparent rule table picks 3 hairstyles and 3 beard templates (e.g. 'oval + low-medium density: textured crop, not slick-back'), each showing the measurement that drove it. 4) Chaining: each hairstyle result URL is the input to the Beard Generator, producing a 3x3 swipeable grid of complete looks. 5) The user picks one and gets at most 3 products, each tied to a measurement (high frizz -> anti-frizz cream; lower density -> matte volumizing paste; high oiliness -> oil-control cleanser), in cosmetic copy with a 'not medical advice' line. 6) A full-screen Barber card with face-shape notes, saved or AirDropped.
youcam_apis: Face Attributes & Ratio (Face Analyzer)
Hair Density Detection
Hair Frizziness Detection
Skin Analysis v2.1 SD (oiliness, pore, skin_type, redness)
Hair Style VTO (template/hair-style)
Beard Style Generator (chained on hairstyle output)
Optional: Hair Color VTO
novelty_vs_competitors: Real overlap: bck-stack/fade-try-on ('Skin check before the cut: Skin Analysis + hairstyle and beard try-on, then book the look', web/MCP); acknowledge it upfront. Lineup differs because it measures hair (density + frizz endpoints) and face ratios and shows the number behind each pick, chains hairstyle output into the Beard Generator for combined looks, and ends in a retail starter kit rather than a booking. Other hair repos (chroma, swatchless, hairloom, ahead, kept, before-it-falls) target women's color or wigs. Grep for frizz, density, groom and barber: 0 hits.

name: AisleCheck: pharmacy beauty-aisle consult with a pharmacist gate and claim linter
one_liner: A phone tool for drugstore beauty advisors. It runs a consented YouCam skin scan, maps results to in-stock cosmetic SKUs with aisle and bay, lints every claim for cosmetic vs drug language, and hard-stops to a pharmacist handoff when a customer reports red-flag symptoms.
target_user: Beauty advisors and pharmacy technicians in drugstore and pharmacy chains working the OTC skincare aisle; the customer is a walk-in shopper at the shelf.
buyer: Retailer (pharmacy/drugstore chain). The KPIs are consult-to-basket rate, pharmacist referrals logged, 'need with no in-stock SKU' merchandising gaps, and a documented compliance trail.
core_flow: 1) Consult mode: the advisor hands over the phone, and the customer reads a plain-language e-consent (no storage, deletion after the result, no identity link). 2) Red-flag triage in 3 taps (painful, bleeding or changing spot? sudden rash or swelling? on a prescription skin medication?). Any yes locks the scan, sends nothing to YouCam, and creates a 'see pharmacist' ticket. 3) Capture with a framing and light-quality gate, then SD Skin Analysis (moisture, oiliness, redness, pore, texture, dark_circle_v2) and Fitzpatrick with mask overlays and confidence notes. 4) Shelf map: concerns map only to this store's in-stock CSV. Each pick shows aisle/bay, the triggering ui_score and linted copy; drug-claim phrases are blocked and OTC drug items (e.g. benzoyl peroxide) carry 'confirm with pharmacist'. Optional Makeup VTO preview of a tinted shelf product. 5) The customer leaves with a QR card (routine + shelf locations, no image); the image is deleted. 6) Manager tab: consults, referrals, attach rate, unmet-need gaps.
youcam_apis: File API (presigned upload) + async task polling
Skin Analysis v2.1 SD (moisture, oiliness, redness, pore, texture, dark_circle_v2, skin_type) with mask PNG overlays
Fitzpatrick skin type (confidence messaging)
Makeup VTO concealer/foundation (optional preview of a tinted shelf product)
novelty_vs_competitors: Honest overlap: Balu-SG/shelfmatch (selfie scan to a routine from one store's catalog plus a seller gap dashboard), DesignMaster-Solutions/shelf-check, Noufalthecoder/ShelfSense, nickillig3-dotcom/skin-to-shelf. Scan-to-store matching and the gap dashboard are mostly ShelfMatch. The differences are the setting and compliance layer: an associate-run flow in a physical pharmacy, a triage gate that refuses to scan and routes to a pharmacist, a cosmetic-vs-OTC-drug claim linter built on FDA intended use, and planogram locations. Grep for pharmacy finds only an unrelated download page. Shares the associate-surface idea with C3 Counter, but C3 is about consent and wipe lifecycle for color/makeup; AisleCheck is about medical-boundary triage for skincare.

name: SwapDesk: returns-counter exchange tool for store associates
one_liner: At the in-store returns counter, the associate scans the returned lipstick, foundation or top and picks the reason. YouCam VTO then shows the returned shade or colorway next to in-stock alternatives on the customer's own face or body. A ledger counts each refund turned into an exchange.
target_user: Store associates and returns-desk staff at beauty and apparel retailers handling in-person returns, including buy-online-return-in-store.
buyer: Retailer. The KPIs are refund-to-exchange save rate, revenue retained per shift, and reason-coded return intelligence by SKU (color vs fit) for merchandising.
core_flow: 1) The associate scans the returned item's barcode (expo-camera) for SKU, price and category, and taps a reason: wrong shade/color, didn't suit me, size/fit, or defective. 2) Routing with honesty guardrails: size/fit gets 'VTO can't judge fit' and a size-exchange checklist, defective follows the normal flow, and only color or suitability reasons continue. 3) Consent on the counter phone, then one photo, with upload starting as soon as the reason is tapped. Beauty: Facial Color Tones measures skin and lip hex, in-stock shades are ranked by CIEDE2000, and Makeup VTO renders the returned shade plus the top 2 alternatives. Apparel: cloth-v4 renders the returned garment plus in-stock colorways. 4) Side-by-side swipe, then the customer chooses Exchange / Store credit / Refund; only a human tap changes money. 5) The ledger records the outcome and value retained, and the photo is deleted. 6) Manager tab: save rate by reason, SKUs returning for color (merchandising flag), exchanges per associate.
youcam_apis: File API (presigned upload) + async task polling
Facial Color Tones analyzer (measured skin/lip hex for shade ranking)
Makeup VTO (lip_color, foundation)
Clothes VTO cloth-v4 (upper/lower/full, auto category)
Skin Analysis v2.1 (optional: skin_type to filter foundation formula)
novelty_vs_competitors: Concept overlap is significant: guptachetan1995/shade-guard (wrong-shade return to exchange; README says the returns desk is a desktop view on sample data and the live YouCam provider is not yet called), 0xNexuz/reconsider (shopper-side reason-aware apparel exchanges with cloth-v4), HyunsikParker/mirrormargin-youcam (returns prevention). The differences are a physical in-store counter on the associate's phone, barcode-in, beauty and apparel in one flow, store-limited inventory, live YouCam calls, and a manager ledger of reason-coded save rates as a merchandising signal. The pitch must acknowledge the overlap and lead with the associate surface and ledger. Lowest novelty of the set.
